claim_boundary: Proof draft for ordinary separated +/-1-framed unlink evaluations with universal-character twists. This does not evaluate a non-separated Yasui braid diagram.

Drinfeld_doubles.first_principle_description: In Rep(D(G)), invertible simples are central flux plus a one-dimensional charge, usually denoted (z, chi) with z in Z(G) and chi a linear character of G. The twist is chi(z). If the relevant invertibles are pure charges (z=1), they are bosons and the split test is baseline.
Drinfeld_doubles.important_caveat: A finite group with nontrivial center can have non-bosonic invertibles in its double. Those can create nonbaseline phases, but still only through the pointed metric group of invertibles.

D_A4.reason_baseline: A4 has trivial center, so the D(A4) invertibles relevant to the Z/3 character directions are pure charges and have twist 1.

quantum_group_categories.first_principle_description: For semisimple U_q(g) modular categories, universal-character twists are represented by simple currents. A separated +/-1 unlink sees only the twists of those simple currents, not the non-pointed integrable representations, F-symbols, R-symbols, or fusion multiplicities.

SU2_k.rule: The nontrivial simple current is label k, with twist exp(pi*i*k/2). Hence k=0 mod 4 is baseline for every character assignment; other k have only a simple-current phase.

main_claim.statement: For any unitary modular category C, a universal-character twist of the ordinary CP2#2CPbar split unlink with framings (+1,-1,-1) depends only on the pointed modular subcategory generated by invertible objects. More explicitly, if a character is represented by an invertible object g, then a +1-framed separated unknot contributes theta_g^{-1} times the ordinary Gauss sum, and a -1-framed separated unknot contributes theta_g times the ordinary Gauss sum. Therefore the three-component split value has ratio theta(g_h)^{-1} theta(g_e1) theta(g_e2).

proof_from_first_principles.step: Universal characters become invertibles in a modular category.
proof_from_first_principles.detail: Nondegeneracy of the S-matrix gives a perfect pairing between invertible objects and the universal grading. Thus any character used in the universal-grading twist may be represented by an invertible simple object g.

proof_from_first_principles.step: The character is monodromy with g.
proof_from_first_principles.detail: For every simple X, define chi_g(X)=S_{g,X}/d_X. The balancing equation for an invertible object gives chi_g(X)=theta_{g tensor X}/(theta_g theta_X).

proof_from_first_principles.step: The +1 Gauss sum collapses by reindexing.
proof_from_first_principles.detail: tau_+(g)=sum_X d_X^2 chi_g(X) theta_X = theta_g^{-1} sum_X d_X^2 theta_{g tensor X}. Tensoring by g permutes simple objects and preserves dimensions, so tau_+(g)=theta_g^{-1} tau_+(1).

proof_from_first_principles.step: The -1 Gauss sum is the dual/unitary conjugate identity.
proof_from_first_principles.detail: In a unitary ribbon category, tau_-(g) is the conjugate counterpart of tau_+(g^{-1}), hence tau_-(g)=theta_g tau_-(1).
The ordinary CP2#2CPbar presentation is a split unlink, so the three component sums multiply. With framings (+1,-1,-1), the total ratio is theta(g_h)^{-1} theta(g_e1) theta(g_e2).

research_consequence.for_current_search: Scanning Uq(g) or D(G) examples on the separated ordinary presentation is not a way to see non-pointed or multiplicity-nonfree structure. It is only a scan of the finite quadratic form on invertible objects.
research_consequence.literal_baseline_test: A candidate is literally baseline for every character assignment exactly when the relevant invertible twists make theta(g_h)^{-1} theta(g_e1) theta(g_e2)=1 for every assignment.
research_consequence.stronger_uselessness_test: Even when nonbaseline phases occur, they are simple-current/pointed phases. They should be treated as ordinary intersection-form data, not as evidence that the full category may distinguish the Yasui exotic presentation.

things_not_yet_proved_here: A full theorem for arbitrary non-separated surgery links and arbitrary integer framings.
A formal identification of the exact Yetter twist convention with the universal-character convention in every premodular/nonmodular case.
A cited classification statement for simple currents of every U_q(g) family.
A cited classification statement for invertible simples of twisted doubles D^omega(G).
